grammar_points.name: 〜ても (temo - even if)

explanation.en:
Expresses "even if" or "even though." The speaker acknowledges a condition but says the result stays the same regardless.

How it works:
Take the て-form (te-form) of a verb and add も (mo). It means "even if [verb happens]."

Example from this song:
巡り巡っても (meguri megutte mo, "Even if time goes round and round")

More examples:
- 雨が降っても行く (ame ga futte mo iku, "I'll go even if it rains")
- 高くても買う (takakute mo kau, "I'll buy it even if it's expensive")
- 何回失敗しても諦めない (nankai shippai shite mo akiramenai, "Even if I fail many times, I won't give up")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 巡る (meguru) → 巡って (megutte, te-form) → 巡っても (megutte mo, "even if it goes around")

explanation.en:
Expresses purpose or a wish: "so that [something happens]" or "in order to." It is used when the desired outcome is not directly under the speaker's control.

How it works:
Place ように (you ni) after the dictionary form (positive) or ない-form (negative) of a verb.

Example from this song:
はぐれないように (hagurenai you ni, "So that we don't get separated")

More examples:
- 忘れないようにメモする (wasurenai you ni memo suru, "I'll take notes so I don't forget")
- 聞こえるように大きい声で話す (kikoeru you ni ookii koe de hanasu, "Speak loudly so it can be heard")
- 遅れないように早く出る (okurenai you ni hayaku deru, "Leave early so as not to be late")

grammar_points.name: 〜んだ (nda - explanatory)

explanation.en:
Adds an explanatory or emphatic tone to a statement. It signals that the speaker is giving a reason, making a strong declaration, or emphasizing their resolve.

How it works:
Attach んだ (nda) after the plain form of a verb, adjective, or noun + な. In casual speech, it often sounds like "It's that..." or adds conviction.

Example from this song:
この手をつなぐんだ (kono te o tsunagu nda, "I WILL hold this hand" - emphatic resolve)

More examples:
- 行くんだ (iku nda, "I'm going! / The thing is, I'm going")
- 好きなんだ (suki na nda, "The truth is, I like you")
- どうして泣いてるんだ (doushite naiteru nda, "Why are you crying?")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: つなぐ (tsunagu) + んだ (nda) → つなぐんだ (tsunagu nda, "I will hold [hands] - emphatic")

grammar_points.name: 〜ながら (nagara - while)

explanation.en:
Expresses doing two actions at the same time: "while doing [X], also doing [Y]." The main action comes at the end of the sentence.

How it works:
Take the masu-stem of a verb and add ながら (nagara). The secondary (background) action gets ながら, and the main action follows.

Example from this song:
つなぎ直しながら (tsunaginaoshi nagara, "While reconnecting hands")

More examples:
- 音楽を聴きながら勉強する (ongaku o kiki nagara benkyou suru, "Study while listening to music")
- 歩きながら話す (aruki nagara hanasu, "Talk while walking")
- コーヒーを飲みながら新聞を読む (koohii o nomi nagara shinbun o yomu, "Read the newspaper while drinking coffee")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: つなぎ直す (tsunaginaosu) → つなぎ直し (tsunaginaoshi, masu-stem) + ながら (nagara) → つなぎ直しながら (tsunaginaoshi nagara)

explanation.en:
A conditional meaning "if." It is used when the speaker takes a hypothetical situation as a premise and then states what would follow.

How it works:
Attach なら (nara) after the plain past form of a verb or the dictionary form. It sets up a condition.

Example from this song:
描いたなら (egaita nara, "If you've envisioned [a dream]")

More examples:
- 暇なら映画を見よう (hima nara eiga o miyou, "If you're free, let's watch a movie")
- 日本に行くなら京都がおすすめ (nihon ni iku nara kyouto ga osusume, "If you go to Japan, I recommend Kyoto")
- 分かったなら早くやって (wakatta nara hayaku yatte, "If you understood, do it quickly")

grammar_points.name: 〜続ける (tsuzukeru - to keep doing)

explanation.en:
An auxiliary verb meaning "to continue doing." Attached to the masu-stem of another verb, it expresses an ongoing, sustained action.

How it works:
Take the masu-stem of a verb and add 続ける (tsuzukeru).

Example from this song:
照らし続けよう (terashi tsuzukeyou, "Let's keep illuminating")

More examples:
- 走り続ける (hashiri tsuzukeru, "to keep running")
- 信じ続ける (shinji tsuzukeru, "to keep believing")
- 練習し続ければ上手になる (renshuu shi tsuzukereba jouzu ni naru, "If you keep practicing, you'll get good")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 照らす (terasu) → 照らし (terashi, masu-stem) + 続ける (tsuzukeru) → 照らし続けよう (terashi tsuzukeyou, "let's keep shining")
